questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: There are a lot of options and rent isn't too bad. But it was difficult to find someone who would accept short term lease. Look on Facebook marketplace and use a vpn to write to people.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I think it's the better option. You can get a nice location and make a relationship to the city itself. And you don't have to pay for meal plan.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Find and read about the classes on McGill website. There is a tool where you can add them to a schedule, do this to see if they overlap. At another page you actually sign up for the courses. You can sometimes use the ratemyprofessor website to read about a prof or a course. There is an add/drop period until around 2 weeks into the semester, that is great! So use it to check out different classes if you are in doubt.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer:
There is an academic advisor for incoming exchange students. For me it was Mary. She is great you can use her.

If you have questions about a course, your prerequisites or the course is full, you can often write the prof.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Almost succesful. But I was satisfied!

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Look in advance and maybe reach out to staff/advisors at the school. The course "levels" 100/200 do not always represent the difficulty of a course. Eg. I thought some 500s would be too difficult for me, so I didn't register. But when I arrived and talked to an advisor, she told me that that specific course was really not too bad, and people from other departments do it. But by then it was full.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
Higher numbers = more difficult. In general! It is not directly applicable. Eg my 250 course was more difficult than my 534 course. Often the "introduction" courses can be surprisingly difficult and the 500's courses can be easy, since they are made for master students who do research on the side. So in general it's hard to tell in advance. Use
ratemyprofessors.com

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: For me less TA hours than I'm used to. Along the way there are quizzes, assignments and midterms that affect your grade.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *

questions.answer: Mont Tremblant and La Mauricie. If you have money and time go to Banff or Jasper national park in September

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The language. But I liked it and learned some French

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Its a multicultural environment, which is very nice.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. I don't think you should do the on campus housing.
2. Many of my fellow exchange students, myself included, found the academic workload at McGill high. For some it was a lot and definitely not what they had hoped for. Don't take too difficult courses
3. Montreal is amazing. Have fun, explore the city. Go in the fall semester! Unless you like it cold :D

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
ratemyprofessors.com
. You can reach out to ucph students who went to McGill before. Find us in the Facebook group "ku studerende I Canada" I think

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: New friendships with other exchange students. I had more time on my hands to chill and explore.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I didn't really talk to people in class like im used to, I was more anonymous. But for one semester it was fine. Could definitely also have done more. The local students tend to be younger, they start their undergrad at 18 yrs. My stay was only 4 months, which is a biiit short but it's fine.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: You should go!!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
